body.statement: In the three-category specialization \(\mathcal E=\{a,b,c_\star\}\), selected trust and full exclusion are separated by a perturbation-stable generic obstruction, and trusting \(c_\star\) yields a strict bound gain on a separate nondegenerate open region. For every parameter choice in \(q^{\rm sep}_{r,s,\tau,\lambda}\), the displayed construction belongs to \(\mathcal Q_{T_0}(p^{\rm sep})\), every observed cell exceeds \(93/5000\), and, for \(x\in\{a,b\}\), every compatibility sum obeys \(p^{{\rm sep},0}_{xy}+p^{{\rm sep},1}_{x,1-y}<57/125\). Full exclusion is impossible because its necessary inequality \(p^{{\rm sep},0}_{c_\star0}+p^{{\rm sep},1}_{c_\star1}\leq1\) fails: the left side is greater than \(2(31/50)(93/100)=2883/2500>1\). Consequently, every armwise normalized \(p'\) satisfying \(\lVert p'-p^{\rm sep}\rVert_\infty<1/200\) is positive and \(T_0\)-compatible, while \(p'^0_{c_\star0}+p'^1_{c_\star1}>2883/2500-2/200>1\), so no such \(p'\) is representable under \(T_1\). Separately, \(p^{\rm gain}\) lies in the relative interior of the \(T_1\)-compatible set and \[ [L_{T_1}(p^{\rm gain}),U_{T_1}(p^{\rm gain})]=[-7/10,7/10]\subsetneq[-4/5,4/5]=[L_{T_0}(p^{\rm gain}),U_{T_0}(p^{\rm gain})]. \] There exists \(\eta_{\rm gain}>0\) such that every armwise normalized table \(p'\) with \(\lVert p'-p^{\rm gain}\rVert_\infty<\eta_{\rm gain}\) remains \(T_1\)-compatible and satisfies \([L_{T_1}(p'),U_{T_1}(p')]\subsetneq[L_{T_0}(p'),U_{T_0}(p')]\).
body.justification: The two explicit witnesses show that selected trust is neither a relabeling of full exclusion nor observationally vacuous relative to trusting only the targets.
body.gap: Song et al. characterize the full-exclusion model, but that result does not cover the displayed selected-trust response law; Gabriel et al. give isolated ternary comparisons without a nondegenerate strict-improvement region.
body.consumer: A LEAP analyst can distinguish rejection of exclusion for an intermediate category from evidence that a separately trusted intermediate category sharpens the low-versus-high interval.
